notes: Every standable surface is a Walk_<material> node, matching the region's contract: the client turns navigation.surfaceNodePrefixes into the layer its downward grounding ray tests.

notes: [royal_archive] Built from concept.json's written subject list and the authored asset pack's names: its own concept board does not decode at all.
[serpent_hatchery] Authored from the asset pack's `ssarathi_hatchery_pool`, which is Ssarathi interior content outside the Archive's ten subjects. No concept art exists for it.
[tenth_mouth] Built from the shared small-room kit: a cut sanctuary in the water manner.
[water_gate_undercut] Built from the shared small-room kit: mouth, throat and chamber, dressed for the region above it.
[lineage_house] Built from the shared small-room kit: a hall with a hearth and a back room for its trade (workshop).

Four insides on one map with blackspace between them, following amethyst_barrens_insides and crownwater_insides. Cells between sections are zero in collision.bin because no Walk_ surface covers them - the void is not drawn, it is simply the absence of floor.
knownLimitations: Not opened in Godot: no client is installable in the build environment, so collision response, navmesh generation, portal transition, LOD and transparency sorting are unverified.
eloria-server has not registered these map keys.
One environment block serves four sections of different character; the per-section lamps carry most of the lighting difference.

The Royal Archive's own concept board does not decode - zero rows, not just the truncated tail every region board has - so its ten subjects were worked from concept.json's written list and the authored asset pack's piece names. There is no panel comparison for it.
The other three sections have no concept art at all and are authored from the region's surface landmarks and its (intact) region board.
